name: NUMA-aware process binding and NPS (NUMA Partitioning Services) on MI300X
workarounds: NPS1 (default): all memory interleaved across all HBM stacks - maximum bandwidth for single-GPU workloads
NPS2: memory partitioned into two pools (one per IOD) - reduces cross-IOD Infinity Fabric traffic
NPS4: memory partitioned into four pools - for CDNA3 MI300X/MI325X with 4 IODs
For inference: NPS1 is recommended for TP=1 workloads; NPS2 may help TP=8 workloads by reducing cross-IOD traffic
notes:
AMD EPYC processors with MI300X GPUs use NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) architecture. Each GPU is connected to one NUMA node via PCIe Gen5 x16. NPS (NUMA Partitioning Services) controls how memory is interleaved across HBM stacks. On MI300X (CDNA3, 4 IODs): NPS1 interleaves across all 8 HBM stacks (maximum bandwidth), NPS2 partitions into 2 pools, NPS4 partitions into 4 pools. On MI350X/MI355X (CDNA4, 2 IODs): NPS1 or NPS2 only. For inference: NPS1 is recommended for TP=1 workloads (each GPU uses its full memory bandwidth). For TP=8 workloads, NPS2 may reduce cross-IOD Infinity Fabric traffic and improve latency. The ROCm documentation recommends binding GPU processes to the local NUMA node using numactl or ROCm's binding tools. AMD's MLPerf submissions use NPS1 with 8 instances of TP=1 for small models. The vLLM blog notes 'NUMA auto-balancing disabled' in their system configuration.
